messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty Alert fired -> PD-3287 · Severity: P1. Alert: gpu-oom-high on cluster-rw-prod-gpu-2. Service: inference-runtime. Symptoms: repeated CUDA OOM (OOM when allocating tensor), kernel reset events. Link: https://pd.example/PD-3287

pagerduty: page fired to schedule: oncall-eng (primary: @ajay)

ajay: acked. I'm on it. Starting triage — pulling logs and stack traces.

maria: seeing a storm of "CUDA out of memory" from pod inference-srv-14 (node gpu-node-07). GPU mem at ~98% before OOMs. OOMs started ~2m ago.

chris: also seeing repeated NVRM Xid messages in dmesg: `NVRM: Xid (256): 31` — likely driver kill/recovery.

ajay: ok. don't reboot node yet. can we shift traffic away from that node and spawn fallback CPU replicas? I want to avoid mass restarts.

sarah: flipping traffic split to fallback model now (inference-runtime -> vCPU-fallback). Should cut tail latencies for user-facing routes.

ops-bot: traffic-split update applied: inference-runtime=80% gpu, 20% vCPU-fallback -> updating to 50/50 as requested

maria: rolling one problematic pod (inference-srv-14) to new node helped temporarily; but another pod on same node OOM'd immediately after restart. Looks like node-level resource leakage.

ajay: running quick gpu memory dump and nvtop output. Pasting snippet: 
```
GPU 0: 16 GB total, used 15.9 GB
Processes: inference-srv-12 (PID 4321) 9.1 GB
           inference-srv-14 (PID 4410) 6.8 GB
```
Looks like two big processes saturating memory.

chris: suspicious that kv-cache growth not bounded after long-running sessions. We've seen similar when prefix caching didn't evict. Checking runtime metrics for cache size.

maria: customer-impact check: nothing hitting 5xx yet, but p50 latency for chat endpoints jumped from 120ms -> 950ms. I see one support ticket: "inference timeout" from customer acme-inc.

ajay: setting alert for 5xxs. For now, scale up fallback replicas and reduce GPU concurrency on that node. I'll apply a temporary limit on max_concurrency=2 for GPU pool.

sarah: deployed concurrency cap and scaled vCPU-fallback replicas x3. Watch the queues.

incident-bot: escalate to SRE on-call in 10m if error-rate doesn't improve.

chris: quick mitigation idea: force eviction of oldest KV-caches per model. I can push a hotfix to runtime to trim caches to 25% immediately. Need a quick canary. Thoughts?

ajay: do it as a canary on one pod first. Command below to trigger cache trim via admin endpoint: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://inference-admin.internal/pods/inference-srv-12/actions/trim_cache -d '{"percent":75}'
```
Apply to pod on node gpu-node-07 -> monitor.

maria: ran trim on inference-srv-12. GPU mem dropped to 6.2GB, pod stabilized. No more immediate OOMs for that process.

chris: good sign. pushing runtime patch to trim-on-all-evict now (non-breaking). I'll open a PR but can hotpatch the running daemonset.

ajay: authorized hotpatch. Keep fallback traffic on until we confirm stability. Also create a PD incident note: root cause suspected: unbounded KV cache growth + driver-level Xid 31 that amplifies OOM.

pagerduty: PD-3287 updated: acknowledged by ajay; assignment: eng-sre (chris).

ops-bot: rolling hotpatch to runtime-daemonset (canary=1/5)

maria: canary patched pod trimmed cache and remained up for 8m with stable mem. No new Xid logs. Two other pods on same node still had elevated usage; I'm trimming them manually.

ajay: starting a short on-call handoff: @ajay handing off to @chris for the deeper SRE follow-up. I'll remain reachable for questions.

chris: taking over. Next steps: 1) full runtime patch rollout; 2) schedule GPU node maintenance if kernel Xid persists; 3) postmortem and evictions playbook update to trim caches automatically when mem high.

maria: customer update: sent quick note to support triage and flagged acme-inc ticket as "possible transient". Will notify if we see 5xxs.

ajay: marking initial mitigation done: low-latency restored for most users; we reduced P1 blast radius. Leaving PD-3287 open for SRE verification. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: PD-3287: status=investigating · next_update_in=15m · assigned=chris

chris: will follow up with a detailed timeline and RCA. Thanks all for the quick triage.

ops-bot: note: added runbook tag `gpu-oom-kv-cache` to PD-3287.

maria: logging final snapshot and artifacts: dmesg, kube-events, nvtop dump, runtime metrics -> uploaded to PD-3287.

chris: closing the immediate escalation. If Xid 31 reappears or mem creeps back up, PD will escalate automatically.
